## Summary
Lenses checked: correctness, silent-failure, tests, comments.
Restore `app/defaults.json` before merge, because the startup path still reads it and will raise. `is_valid_port` also rejects port 65535, and `load_config` hides read and parse failures.

## Changes
This pull request adds `is_valid_port`, `load_config` (which can use `ujson` when it is installed) and `normalize_host`, and adds millisecond support to `parse_timeout`, with tests for each. It also deletes `app/defaults.json` and adds `docs/reviewer.md` and a test fixture.

## Critical
- app/defaults.json:1 [base] — correctness — Restore defaults.json or update load_defaults — Any call to `load_defaults()` now raises `FileNotFoundError`, because the stale `app/startup.py:6` still reads `Path(__file__).with_name("defaults.json")`. Nothing in the pull request replaces this file. — Every code path that loads application defaults crashes at startup. — Fix: Keep `app/defaults.json`, or change `app/startup.py:6` to use the new config source in the same pull request.

## Important
- app/parse.py:22 — correctness — Accept port 65535 in is_valid_port — `is_valid_port(65535)` returns `False` because `0 < p < 65535` excludes the upper bound, but the docstring says "usable TCP port (1-65535)". — Configurations that use port 65535 are wrongly rejected, and no test checks the upper bound. — Fix: `0 < p <= 65535`
- app/parse.py:30 — silent-failure — Stop swallowing all errors in load_config — A missing file, a permission error or malformed JSON all return `{}` because of `except Exception: return {}`. There is no log, no caller signal and no comment saying the fallback is intended. — An operator with a typo in the config path or a broken config file runs silently on empty settings and has nothing to diagnose. — Fix: Catch only `FileNotFoundError` if a missing file should mean empty config, and let parse and permission errors propagate or log them.

## Suggestions
- app/parse.py:35 — comments — Align normalize_host docstring with empty-input return — `normalize_host("")` returns `""`, but the docstring says "returns None when h is empty". The code at line 37 is `return ""`. — A caller who follows the docstring and checks `is None` treats an empty host as valid.
- app/parse.py:40 — tests — Test the trailing-dot branch of normalize_host — No test covers stripping the trailing dot; `test_normalize_host_lowercases` passes `"Example.COM"`, which has no trailing dot. — A regression in FQDN suffix stripping, for example `"example.com."`, would pass the test suite.
